summary: This bill bars all federal agencies from taking any action or spending funds that recognizes or implies recognition of the Taliban-controlled Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan as the legitimate government, requires the Secretary of State to designate that entity a state sponsor of terrorism, and requires designating the Taliban itself as a foreign terrorist organization.

scores.thoughts: Section 3(b) explicitly prohibits obligating or expending federal funds from State, USAID, or DoD for any actions that would extend recognition to the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan. This creates a narrow but direct restriction on certain government expenditures, pushing slightly toward reduced spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare policy or systems.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms or gun regulations.

Section 5 requires designation of the Taliban as a foreign terrorist organization under the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1189). This has secondary effects on immigration admissibility and visas for Taliban members or affiliates, producing a minor restrictive impact.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion or reproductive rights.
Section 3(b) bars use of Department of Defense funds for recognition-related actions. This is a narrow limitation on DoD expenditures but does not alter overall military spending levels or policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental regulation or climate policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs or social safety net policies.
The bill contains no provisions related to education policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
The bill contains no provisions related to domestic criminal justice, sentencing, or policing.

Section 4 designates the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan as a state sponsor of terrorism, triggering export controls and sanctions under multiple statutes (Export Control Reform Act, Arms Export Control Act, etc.). This imposes trade restrictions, producing a minor protectionist effect.
The bill contains no provisions addressing deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ rights or protections.

Section 3(b) prohibits use of State Department and USAID funds for any policy extending recognition to the Taliban regime. This directly constrains foreign assistance channels that could imply recognition, producing a moderate restrictive effect on aid policy toward Afghanistan.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting, elections, or election integrity.
The bill contains no provisions related to technology regulation or data privacy.
The bill contains no provisions related to labor, unions, or worker protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious liberty or anti-discrimination law.
